items.actClause: AN ACT to amend chapter 581 of the laws of 2005, amending the local finance law relating to statutory installment bonds, in relation to extending the effectiveness thereof
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S6989

TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend chapter 581 of the laws of 2005,
amending the local finance law relating to statutory installment
bonds, in relation to extending the effectiveness thereof

Purpose of the Bill:

The bill would extend for three years to September 30, 2017 provisions
relating to statutory installment bonds issued to the New York State
Environmental Facilities Corporation ("EFC").

Summary of Provisions:

Section 1 of the bill would extend the "sunset" provision of Section 2
of Chapter 581 of the Laws of 2005, thereby extending until September
30, 2017 the provisions of Local Finance Law ("LFL") § 62.10(c) which
authorize local governments to issue statutory installment bonds in an
amount not to exceed $20 million to EFC at a fixed rate or, if issued
in serial maturities, at a set rate for each individual maturity.

Section 2 of the bill provides for an immediate effective date.

Existing Law:

LFL § 62.10(c) allows municipalities to issue a single statutory
installment bond for the full principal amount, not to exceed $20
million, to EFC at a fixed rate or, if issued in serial maturities, at
a set rate for each individual maturity. Under existing law, LFL
62.10(c) will be deemed repealed as of September 30, 2014.

Prior Legislative History:

LFL § 62.10(c) was extended until September 30, 2011 by Chapter 213 of
the Laws of 2008, and until September 30, 2014 by Chapter 69 of the
Laws of 2011.

Statement in Support:

EFC promotes environmental quality by providing low cost capital and
expert technical assistance to municipalities, businesses and State
agencies for environmental projects in New York State. In this role,
EFC administers the Clean Water State Revolving Fund ("CWSRF") and the
Drinking Water State Revolving Fund ("DWSRF"). Under these revolving
fund programs, EFC offers both leveraged and direct loans.

As of November 30, 2012, EFC has issued approximately $15.0 billion in
State Revolving Fund Bonds under the CWSRF program and the DWSRF
program to fund loans to local governments and public benefit
corporations. Before 2005, in accordance with LFL, when a borrower
receiving an EFC financing issued serial bonds to EFC for each
maturity; i.e., for a 20 year financing, EFC would receive 20 separate
bonds from the community. The issuance of serial bonds caused EFC, and
those providing trustee services, excessive servicing cost and
substantial time in handling and processing of multiple bonds. For
example, for EFC pooled financings, since most loans from the State
Revolving Fund are for periods of 20 years, EFC would receive at loan


closing up to 20 separate bonds. For pooled financings, where 30 to 50
borrowers may participate at one time, this would require receiving
600 to 1000 separate individual bonds.  This process also resulted in
unnecessary bonding costs to borrowing entities.

A single debt instrument for financings at or under $20 million, such
as a statutory installment bond, reduces the costs associated with
printing, processing and storage. Reduced paper usage also achieves
environmental benefits, while also reducing the chance of error
associated with multiple printed bonds. This simplified approach also
benefits borrowers in making the financing process more "user
friendly" while enhancing the efficient preparation and execution of
the bonds. Additional allowances for either a fixed or, if issued in
serial maturities, at a set rate of interest, for each individual
maturity, will enable financing options more reflective of the
budgetary realities of the borrowing entity.

Budget Implications:

This bill would have no budget implications to the State but would
provide greater flexibility in local government and public benefit
corporation financing options, while reducing costs associated with
the issuance and sale of bonds to EFC.

Local Impact:

None.

Effective date:

The bill would take effect immediately.
